question.prompt:
If \(X,\) \(Y,\) and \(Z\) are different digits, then the largest possible \(3\)-digit sum for

\[\begin{array}{cr} & XXX \\ & YX \\ + & X \\ \hline \end{array}\]

has the form

solutions.explanation:
The requirement that the sum have three digits rules out \(X=9\). Even the first and last addends would then give
\[
999+9=1008,
\]
which already has four digits. Thus \(X\leq8\).

It follows that \(XXX\) is at most 888, \(YX\) is at most 98, and the last addend is at most 8. Therefore the entire sum is at most
\[
888+98+8=994.
\]
These three upper bounds are attained together by choosing \(X=8\) and \(Y=9\). The result is 994, so we can take \(Z=4\), which is different from both 8 and 9.

Thus the largest three-digit sum is \(994=YYZ\), choice \(\text{D}\).
solutions.title: Bound each addend
